punchline: Houston said the burn forgave most errors, so the crew only had to be exact once.
thirty_sec: About 105 hours into Apollo 13, with the lunar module's computer off, Haise and Lovell aligned by the Sun and Earth's day-night line, burned the descent engine by hand for 7.4 feet per second, and then trimmed it to the 7.6 Houston wanted.
question: Which part of the job you are about to hand over has more room for error than the person doing it believes?
key_contrast: Name what the job forgives and what it does not.
